profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a public-interest law organization preparing a joint submission for a state legislative hearing on a women's economic rights bill that draws on Martha Nussbaum's capabilities framework and comparative examples from India. The legal policy team and the litigation support team need to align on interfaces between a policy memorandum, a constitutional framing section, and an appendix of field narratives from partner NGOs. The agenda is to confirm who is producing which sections, what version of the hearing packet each person is working from, what 'cleared' material can be shared externally, and what must be included in the final packet sent to the coalition lead by Thursday. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on handoffs, drafting status, and the shared source bundle for the hearing submission.

members.name: Asha Mehta
members.expertise: Comparative constitutional law, gender justice, legislative testimony drafting
members.background: Asha leads policy drafting at a nonprofit legal advocacy center and previously worked on constitutional equality submissions in India and South Africa before moving into U.S. state-level legislative advocacy.
members.private_state: She wants the hearing packet to look polished and normatively coherent so coalition partners treat her team as the intellectual lead, and she is quietly worried that factual inconsistencies or improperly attributed field material will undermine the organization's credibility.
hidden_assumptions: When a document is described as the 'brief,' that means the external-facing hearing packet consisting of testimony, citations, and appendices in near-final form.
If material is said to be 'cleared,' that means client-identifying details have already been scrubbed and the material is safe to circulate to the full coalition list.

The 'India examples' in this project refer to the translated NGO case summaries from the recent Rajasthan and Karnataka partner packets, because those are the only examples she has seen folded into hearing drafts.
A section is 'ready' once the legal framing is citation-complete and internally sign-offable, even if copyedits and formatting remain.

members.name: Daniel Ruiz
members.expertise: Fact development, witness coordination, NGO partner intake, document management
members.background: Daniel coordinates source collection from community partners and legal aid clinics, having previously worked as a paralegal managing declarations, redactions, and multilingual evidence packets in impact litigation.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid delaying partner relationships by repeatedly asking for new approvals, and he is mainly focused on moving source material efficiently into the packet without creating extra process bottlenecks.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'brief,' they usually mean the internal working memo plus source bundle that the drafters use, not the polished hearing packet sent outside the office.
If material is 'cleared,' that means the partner organization has approved the substance for advocacy use, even if names, locations, or quotes still need final redaction before broad circulation.

The 'India examples' refers to the full set of source materials associated with the Nussbaum framing memo, including older Andhra Pradesh affidavits in the shared drive because they are tagged under the same project folder.
A section is 'ready' once the substantive content is assembled and usable by the next workstream, even if formal legal citations and final edits are still outstanding.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to getting material into 'the brief' by Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the near-final external hearing packet that will circulate to coalition partners and legislative staff.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the internal drafting bundle/work product from which the policy team will build the final hearing packet.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In legal workplaces 'brief' is a routine shorthand for several adjacent documents, and because both are discussing the same project timeline, each hears the phrase as naturally referring to their own document layer.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that only 'cleared' narratives should be included.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes 'cleared' means redacted, attribution-approved, and safe for distribution beyond the organization.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes 'cleared' means the partner approved advocacy use in principle, with technical redactions to be handled later in final packaging.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are trying to be careful and ethical with sensitive stories, so the shared word signals diligence rather than a point of possible divergence.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss attaching the 'India examples' to support the capabilities framework section.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the recent translated NGO summaries from Rajasthan and Karnataka already excerpted in the policy memo.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the broader project folder labeled India materials, including older Andhra Pradesh affidavits and intake summaries.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds specific enough because both know the project's comparative-law theme centers on India, and neither expects there to be multiple internally recognized subsets under that label.

misalignment_points.topic: Scope of the constitutional framing section
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree Daniel will send over material for the 'constitutional framing section.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this section is limited to constitutional principles and comparative rights language, with factual narratives staying in the appendix.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the constitutional framing section also includes short illustrative fact boxes drawn from partner narratives to show how the principles land in lived experience.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The section title plausibly covers both doctrinal framing and embedded examples, and each thinks the other shares the standard drafting convention they are used to.

When I say the brief, I'm thinking of the packet that could practically go out, not another internal bundle.
